chunks: "Enter the gates of Hell," they will be told, "and there abide for ever." How grievous a destination for the haughty!

key_terms.أَبْوَابَ: Gates (plural of door, referring to the entrances of Hell)
key_terms.الْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ: The haughty / the arrogant (those who display pride and superiority)
key_terms.جَهَنَّمَ: Hell (a specific name for the Fire)
key_terms.فَبِئْسَ: How evil / what a bad (exclamatory phrase)

ai.seo_question: What is the eternal fate of the arrogant (al-mutakabbirun) according to this Quranic verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the concept of *al-Kibr* (arrogance) as the root of all sins, particularly referencing the Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) instruction to enter through the gates corresponding to one's specific sin. The phrase 'evil is the dwelling' (*bi'sa al-mathwa*) serves as a divine rebuke to those who, like Iblis, refused to submit to God's command due to pride, emphasizing that their eternal punishment is a direct consequence of their self-exaltation.
